title: Pousser et tirer - découvrir les forces
oneGoal: Students will explore pushing and pulling as two different types of forces through hands-on play and movement
decisionPoints: Which classroom objects are safest for push/pull exploration?
Should we focus on body movements or object movements first?
Are students ready for comparing push vs pull effectiveness?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes push and pull as basic forces through direct physical experience and play
realWorldConnection: How children naturally push playground swings and pull wagon handles in their daily play

title: Force forte, force faible
oneGoal: Students will discover that forces can be strong or weak and observe how force strength affects movement
decisionPoints: How can we make force strength visible and measurable for young learners?
Should we use the same objects or different objects for force comparisons?
Are students ready for predicting outcomes based on force strength?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by introducing force intensity while practicing push/pull vocabulary through strength variations
realWorldConnection: Understanding why some doors are harder to open and why gentle pushes move things slowly

title: Faire rouler - les objets qui roulent
oneGoal: Students will investigate how pushing and pulling forces make round objects roll and move in different ways
decisionPoints: Which round objects are safest and most effective for rolling experiments?
Should we focus on rolling speed, rolling distance, or rolling direction?
Are students ready for controlling rolling direction through force application?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by applying forces to specific objects (wheels/balls) while introducing directional control concepts
realWorldConnection: How balls roll when kicked and how toy cars move when pushed in different directions

title: Expérience de roulement
oneGoal: Students will conduct simple experiments to test how different forces affect rolling distance and speed
decisionPoints: What materials create the clearest rolling distance demonstrations?
Should we measure distance with non-standard or standard units?
Are students ready for hypothesis-making about force and distance relationships?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by conducting structured experiments while introducing measurement and scientific observation
realWorldConnection: Testing how hard to throw a ball to reach a friend or how gently to roll a toy to a sibling

title: Faire glisser sur différentes surfaces
oneGoal: Students will explore how different surfaces affect the movement of objects when pushed or pulled
decisionPoints: Which surface types provide the clearest movement differences?
Should we test sliding with the same object on different surfaces?
Are students ready for discussions about friction without using the term?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by introducing surface variables while exploring how environment affects force effectiveness
realWorldConnection: Why sleds work better on snow than grass and why some floors are slippery

title: Les roues nous aident - introduction aux machines simples
oneGoal: Students will discover that wheels make moving objects easier and are examples of simple machines that help us
decisionPoints: Which wheeled objects are most familiar and accessible to students?
Should we compare with-wheels vs without-wheels using same objects?
Are students ready for identifying wheels in their environment?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by introducing helpful machines concept while connecting wheels to easier movement
realWorldConnection: How shopping carts, strollers, and wheelchairs help people move heavy things easily

title: Expérience: avec et sans roues
oneGoal: Students will experiment with moving objects with and without wheels to understand how wheels reduce effort needed
decisionPoints: What objects can safely be tested both with and without wheels?
Should we focus on effort needed or distance achieved?
Are students ready for making predictions before testing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by conducting comparative experiments while understanding wheels as helpful tools
realWorldConnection: Comparing dragging a heavy box versus rolling it on a dolly

title: Les leviers - soulever avec un bâton
oneGoal: Students will explore how levers help us lift heavy objects using less force through simple lever activities
decisionPoints: What safe fulcrum and lever materials are available for Grade 1 exploration?
Should we focus on lifting effectiveness or balancing concepts?
Are students ready for understanding how levers multiply force?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by introducing another simple machine while connecting to force multiplication concepts
realWorldConnection: How playground seesaws work and why people use pry bars to open stuck lids

title: Expérience de leviers
oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments with makeshift levers to lift objects and compare effort with and without levers
decisionPoints: Which lever experiments are safest and most demonstrative for young children?
Should we use identical objects or vary the objects being lifted?
Are students ready for discussing why levers work without complex physics?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by conducting hands-on lever experiments while reinforcing simple machine benefits
realWorldConnection: Understanding how bottle openers, scissors handles, and wheelbarrows make work easier

title: Les plans inclinés - rendre les pentes utiles
oneGoal: Students will discover how ramps and slopes help move objects up to higher places with less force
decisionPoints: What ramp materials and angles are safest for classroom exploration?
Should we focus on ease of movement or height achievement?
Are students ready for comparing steep vs gentle ramp effectiveness?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by introducing inclined planes while connecting to reducing force needed for lifting
realWorldConnection: How wheelchair ramps help people and why trucks use loading ramps instead of lifting

title: Expérience de rampes
oneGoal: Students will experiment with different ramp angles and surfaces to find the most effective ways to move objects upward
decisionPoints: Which ramp angles provide clear differences in ease of movement?
Should we test multiple objects or focus on one object with various ramps?
Are students ready for systematic testing and recording results?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by conducting structured ramp experiments while practicing scientific observation methods
realWorldConnection: Testing how steep a ramp can be for bike riding or moving furniture into a truck

title: Les poulies - soulever avec des cordes
oneGoal: Students will explore simple pulleys and discover how they help lift objects by changing force direction
decisionPoints: What safe pulley systems can be created or demonstrated in the classroom?
Should we focus on lifting ease or directional change of force?
Are students ready for understanding how pulleys redirect pulling force?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by introducing pulleys while connecting to force direction and lifting assistance
realWorldConnection: How flagpoles work and why construction sites use cranes with pulleys to lift heavy materials

title: Identifier les machines simples autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify examples of simple machines (wheels, levers, ramps, pulleys) in their classroom and daily environment
decisionPoints: Which simple machines are most visible and recognizable in the school environment?
Should we focus on one type of machine per exploration or survey all types?
Are students ready for explaining how identified machines help people?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by applying simple machine knowledge to recognize real-world applications
realWorldConnection: Finding wheels on chairs, levers in scissors, ramps at school entrances, and pulleys on blinds

title: Construire nos propres machines simples
oneGoal: Students will design and build simple machines using classroom materials to solve movement problems
decisionPoints: What construction materials are safe and effective for Grade 1 simple machine building?
Should students work individually or in collaborative groups?
Are students ready for design challenges or should they follow guided construction?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by applying all simple machine learning to create functional devices
realWorldConnection: Building ramps for toy cars, levers for moving classroom supplies, or pulleys for lifting objects

title: Tester nos machines - est-ce que ça marche?
oneGoal: Students will test their constructed simple machines and evaluate their effectiveness in making movement easier (extension)
decisionPoints: What testing criteria help students evaluate machine effectiveness?
Should we focus on successful function or comparative improvement?
Are students ready for redesigning machines that don't work well?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - evaluates student-made machines while reinforcing problem-solving and design thinking
realWorldConnection: Testing whether homemade machines actually make tasks easier like professional tools do

title: Améliorer nos machines
oneGoal: Students will modify and improve their simple machines based on testing results and new ideas (extension)
decisionPoints: Which improvements are most achievable with available materials and time?
Should students redesign from scratch or modify existing machines?
Are students ready for collaborative improvement sharing and helping?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - advances to iterative design while reinforcing engineering thinking processes
realWorldConnection: How inventors improve their designs and why tools and machines keep getting better over time

title: Forces et mouvements dans les jeux
oneGoal: Students will analyze playground games and sports to identify forces and simple machines in recreational activities (extension)
decisionPoints: Which playground activities show the clearest examples of forces and simple machines?
Should we focus on games students know well or introduce new examples?
Are students ready for making connections between play and physics concepts?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - applies force and machine concepts to familiar recreational contexts
realWorldConnection: Understanding the science behind swings, slides, seesaws, and ball games they play every day

title: Inventeur de machines - résoudre des problèmes
oneGoal: Students will identify everyday problems and design simple machines to solve them like real inventors (extension)
decisionPoints: Which everyday problems are most relatable and solvable for Grade 1 students?
Should students choose their own problems or work from teacher-provided challenges?
Are students ready for presenting their inventions and explaining how they work?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - advances to creative problem-solving while applying all unit learning
realWorldConnection: How real inventors see problems in daily life and create machines to make life easier

title: Exposition de machines simples
oneGoal: Students will create an exhibition showcasing their simple machines and explaining how forces make movement possible (extension)
decisionPoints: What exhibition format best allows students to demonstrate their learning?
Should students present individually or in collaborative groups?
Are students ready for teaching others about forces and simple machines?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - culminates learning through public demonstration and science communication
realWorldConnection: How science museums and invention fairs help people learn about machines and technology

title: Célébration des petits ingénieurs
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their engineering achievements with families by demonstrating forces and simple machines (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration highlight each student's understanding of forces and movement?
Should we include interactive demonstrations or display completed projects?
What activities best show families how students learned about simple machines?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates complete engineering unit while building community connections and STEM confidence
realWorldConnection: How engineering celebrations help families understand the science and technology that make daily life easier
